what: Normative reference model (mean / SD corridor) — NormativeModel
title: Normative reference model (mean / SD corridor) — NormativeModel
text: Builds reusable description normative reference — expected mean sd measurement, optionally stratified covariates age, sex task. model can scalar (one mean/sd), waveform (per-timepoint mean/sd vectors, e.g. 101-point gait-cycle corridor), stratified table (data.frame strata columns plus mean/sd optional time column), lookup function function(age, sex, task) returning list(mean, sd, time). table/function forms let normative database drive model; database available inline scalar/waveform/table spec degrades gracefully interface.

title: Normative reference model (mean / SD corridor) — NormativeModel
code: NormativeModel(   mean,   sd = NULL,   by = c("age", "sex", "task"),   source = NULL,   time = NULL )

title: Normative reference model (mean / SD corridor) — NormativeModel
text: mean Numeric scalar vector (reference mean / waveform), data.frame stratified norms (must contain mean sd columns, plus strata columns optional time column), lookup function(age, sex, task) returning list(mean=, sd=, time=). sd Numeric scalar vector length mean (recycled length 1). Required numeric form; ignored table / function forms. Character vector naming stratification columns/arguments (default c("age", "sex", "task")); data.frame defaults narrowed columns actually present. source Optional character string describing normative source (citation), used default plot title. time Optional numeric vector (length mean) giving x-axis (e.g. % gait cycle) waveform model.

title: Normative reference model (mean / SD corridor) — NormativeModel
text: object class "NormativeModel".

title: Normative reference model (mean / SD corridor) — NormativeModel
code: # scalar norm (e.g. comfortable gait speed for a stratum) m <- NormativeModel(mean = 1.30, sd = 0.15, source = "Bohannon 1997") normativeZScore(1.00, m) #> [1] -2  # waveform norm (101-point knee-flexion corridor) wf <- NormativeModel(mean = sin(seq(0, pi, length.out = 101)),                      sd = rep(0.1, 101), time = 0:100)

what: Classify pre-to-post change against MDC and MCID thresholds — annotateChange
title: Classify pre-to-post change against MDC and MCID thresholds — annotateChange
text: Annotates set paired (pre, post) outcome scores Minimal Detectable Change (MDC) Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) thresholds, classifying change "change" (within measurement error), "detectable (>MDC)" (real change clears measurement error) "clinically meaningful (>MCID)". Thresholds compared absolute change boundary-inclusive (change exactly equal MDC "detectable"). direction benefit tracked separately decrease--good metrics (pain, timed tests) handled correctly.

title: Classify pre-to-post change against MDC and MCID thresholds — annotateChange
code: annotateChange(pre, post, mdc, mcid, direction = "increase")

title: Classify pre-to-post change against MDC and MCID thresholds — annotateChange
text: pre, post Numeric vectors pre- post-intervention scores (one element per metric); may named label metrics. mdc, mcid Numeric MDC / MCID thresholds (positive), scalar recycled across metrics vector matching pre. Obtain MDC PhysioCore::mdc() (PhysioMoCap::mdc()); MCID instrument's anchor-based value. direction Benefit direction, "increase" (higher better, default) "decrease" (lower better); scalar applied metrics vector matching pre.

title: Classify pre-to-post change against MDC and MCID thresholds — annotateChange
text: data.frame class "change_annotation" columns metric, pre, post, change (signed post - pre), improvement (signed positive = beneficial), mdc, mcid, exceeds_mdc, exceeds_mcid, improved, direction classification. metric missing pre post yields NA change classification: missingness propagated rather silently reported "  change".

title: Classify pre-to-post change against MDC and MCID thresholds — annotateChange
text: de Vet HCW et al. (2006). Minimally important change determined visual method. Qual Life Res; Shrout & Fleiss (1979) SEM underlying MDC.

title: Classify pre-to-post change against MDC and MCID thresholds — annotateChange
code: annotateChange(pre = c(fma = 20, pain = 7),                post = c(fma = 31, pain = 4),                mdc = c(5.2, 1.0), mcid = c(9, 2),                direction = c("increase", "decrease")) #> <change_annotation> 2 metric(s) #>  metric change mdc mcid                classification #>     fma     11 5.2    9 clinically meaningful (>MCID) #>    pain     -3 1.0    2 clinically meaningful (>MCID)

text: Summarises nonoverlap / trend effect sizes two-phase (/B) single- case series, delegating peer-reviewed estimators PhysioClinStats: Percentage Non-overlapping Data (percentage), Nonoverlap Pairs, baseline-trend-corrected Tau-U bounded tau-b ("scan") form.

code: scedStats(data, phase, improvement = c("increase", "decrease"))

title: PhysioReport 0.1.1
text: Fixed DOCX report generation current officer/rvg: rvg removed editable vector (DrawingML) graphics Word bodies (rvg::dml() now PowerPoint/Excel-, body_add_vg() defunct), officer::body_add() method dml object. Plots now embedded officer’s supported body_add_gg() (rasterised image). Fixes docx render test.

title: PhysioReport 0.1.0
text: Initial release standalone package x-biosignal physiological signal ecosystem. PhysioReport provides parameterized, bilingual, colorblind-safe building blocks clinical reports (gait, HRV, EMG) normative overlays MDC/MCID-annotated change.

title: PhysioReport 0.1.0
text: Bilingual (Japanese / English) report labels via physioLabel(), resolves label key localized string. dictionary lives UTF-8 data file (inst/extdata/labels.csv), keeping R source ASCII, unknown keys fall back key partial dictionaries never break report. Clinical agreement visualization plotBlandAltman(): draws Bland-Altman plot (mean vs. difference paired measurements) bias limit--agreement reference lines. Statistics computed PhysioCore::blandAltman(), plotted lines exactly match returned bias limits agreement, labels/axes localized physioLabel().

title: PhysioReport 0.1.0
text: Consistent, accessible report styling via reportTheme(), thin wrapper around shared colorblind-safe PhysioCore::theme_physio() every report uses ecosystem theme palette.
